java.verifier: JBMC 6.11.0, bounded. ASSURANCE.md listed Java's R4 route as OpenJML/KeY; neither was ever attempted, and F014 established that the route that IS available -- JBMC over the compiled bytecode -- hits the same three defects the Kotlin corner hits, in the language those defects were reduced to. `impls/java/verification` now carries the twin of the Kotlin corner's obligation set, measured rather than assumed (F034): 7 of the 15 obligations are decidable and 8 carry a recorded JBMC limit, the same partition as Kotlin's. `calibrate -impls java -rungs R4` drives `tools/cmd/jbmc verify`, whose denominator is the 7 decidable obligations
java.status: written against the S_obs contract; R0 54/54 byte-exact, canary sweep 4/4 rejected. No build tool and no dependencies: plain javac against JDK 17, serving HTTP/1.1 on a raw ServerSocket (the JDK HttpServer is not total over the request target)

kotlin.verifier: JBMC 6.11.0, bounded. No deductive verifier exists for Kotlin (ASSURANCE.md), so R4 here is bounded model checking rather than proof, and 8 of the 15 obligations are undecidable by a JBMC defect rather than by anything about Kotlin (F014). `calibrate -impls kotlin -rungs R4` drives `tools/cmd/jbmc verify`, whose denominator is the 7 decidable obligations
kotlin.status: written against the S_obs contract; R0 56/56 byte-exact, canary sweep 4/4 rejected. No build tool and no library dependencies: kotlinc 2.4.10 emits a self-contained jar (-include-runtime bundles kotlin-stdlib), serving HTTP/1.1 on a raw ServerSocket for the same reason the Java corner does -- the JDK HttpServer is not total over the request target, and a Kotlin HTTP framework would have re-introduced the F008 routing defect
